newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIA POST RECORD PROFIT

Australia Post says its dividend to the Government will rise nearly 19 per cent, to more than 142 million dollars, following its record profit of more than 344-million dollars for the past financial year.
Australia Post says it's a revenue boost of nearly five-per-cent.
The company is claiming a four-per cent productivity increase as one of the main reasons for the rise in profit, along with cuts to labor costs.
However the wage bill remains one of the biggest costs to the national mail carrier, making up 60-per cent of total outlays.
PM SAYS MEDIA INQUIRY WILL BE TRANSPARENT
Prime Minister John Howard says whatever method of inquiry is adopted to review cross-media ownership laws, people will be able to put their views.
There's speculation the Government will back away from its committment to hold a comprehensive public review of the laws, in favour of a discussion paper which outlines options for regulation.
But Mr Howard has told Perth radio 6PR, the Coalition made it clear before the election there'd be a review to look at the cross media rules which have become outdated by the advances in technology.
He says any review would be transparent.
NATIONAL PARTY PLAYS AUDIENCE TO PAULINE HANSON
The National Party in Queensland has confirmed outspoken Federal Independent, Pauline Hanson, addressed a meeting of one of its branches in Brisbane last night.
Ms Hanson made the speech the same day Federal National Party leader Tim Fischer criticised her comments about Asian immigration.
Ms Hanson spoke to the National's Mansfield-Mount Gravatt branch in Brisbane's southern suburbs last night.
NSW PREMIER SAYS GOOD START TO BANNED GUNS BUY-BACK
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has described taking delivery of the first truckload of banned firearms, bought back by the government, as a good start.
Mr Carr and Police Minister Paul Whelan took delivery of the firearms under a tougher regime of gun laws.
The guns belonged to a licensed firearm dealer, one of about 60 who've applied for banned weapons to be collected.
SEAFOOD SHORTAGE COULD LEAD TO CONFLICT
A conference underway in Canberra has been told of the potential for a severe shortage of seafood in the world that could cause major conflicts between countries.
Professor Nigel Forteath from the University of Tasmania has told the 65th ANZAAS congress that by the year 2000 the demand for fish will be in excess of 120 million tonnes.
Professor Forteath says urgent action is needed to move towards sustainable aquaculture, to meet the shortfall and protect marine resources before they're destroyed.
BLACKHAWK INQUIRY CONTINUES
One of the planners of an ill-fated military exercise in which 18 servicemen were killed, has told an inquiry there were no major safety concerns in the planning of the exercise.
Fifteen SAS soldiers and three aircrew were killed when two
Blackhawk helicopters collided during counter-terrorist training near Townsville in June.
The Sergeant told the Military Board of Inquiry in Perth today that the exercise had been planned well before June and that he was confident with the briefing that had been given.
He said he would not change any aspect of the exercise if similar training was held in the future.
NEW TECHNOLOGY MAY REDUCE SKIN CANCER
The incidence of skin cancer may be reduced with the advent of a new technique called surface microscopy which enables GPs to detect and diagnose melanomas within minutes.
Scientists at the 65th ANZAAS conference in Canberra have been told the new technique should be available to general practitioners within a few years.
The CSIRO's Mark Berman says surface microscopy, through digital image analysis, will provide an almost immediate diagnosis.
GOVERNMENT SUSPENDS LUPIN IMPORTS
The Federal Government has suspended lupin seed imports because of concern about further outbreaks of the disease, lupin anthracnose.
Primary Industries minister John Anderson says the suspension applies immediately for the next six weeks, while all lupin growing states test for the disease and consider control measures.
He says the decision was made after personal representations from the West Australian Government and state Farmers' Federation.

The minister says seed for consumption can only be imported if it has been processed in such a way that it cannot germinate and small amounts of seed for sowing will be allowed if tests show the seed is disease-free.
MORE CHANCE OF DYING FROM ASTEROID THAN PLANE CRASH
A Canberra science conference has been told the chance of dying from an asteroid strike is greater than the possibility of being killed in a plane crash.
Doctor Duncan Steele, a space researcher from Adelaide University, says the influence of cosmic impact, such as asteroids, is now considered a major factor in the evolution of the earth's geology.
Doctor Steele today addressed the ANZAAS conference, a gathering of Australian and New Zealand scientists.
